# Results — Study 519 (Net-Share-Issuance)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The factor — **firms that issue
shares (dilute) underperform; firms that buy back outperform** (Pontiff-Woodgate 2008;
Daniel-Titman composite issuance) — tested as a clean **annual cross-sectional sort**. The
signal is each firm's year-over-year change in **split-adjusted** shares outstanding (so a 4-for-1
split does not masquerade as 300% issuance); we go **long the low-issuance** tail (buybacks),
**short the high-issuance** tail (dilution), and hold the **next** year (one execution lag).
Offline & deterministic given the cache; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes + `get_shares_full` shares outstanding, split-adjusted via the firm's split history (public, no key) |
| As-of | **2026-06-26** (cache fingerprint `4c0f2b42cabf`) |
| Basket | **40** large-cap **survivor** names across sectors (an explicit, named survivor set) |
| Panel | year-ends **2014 → 2025** (12 year-end bars); **9** usable long-short formation years (**2016 → 2024**, each held into the next year) |
| Signal | net issuance = `shares_adj[t] / shares_adj[t-1] − 1` (split-adjusted; + = dilution, − = buyback) |
| Sort / entry | bottom/top **30%** by issuance, equal-weight; **1-year** execution lag (form at year-end *t*, hold *t→t+1*) |
| Costs | one-way **10 bps** × both legs × full annual turnover + **50 bps** short-leg borrow |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The 40 names are large caps **still trading in
> 2026**, so the basket is survivorship-selected (the firms that diluted into oblivion or were
> acquired are absent — both ways of upward-biasing the *issuers* leg, which works *against*
> finding the published effect, but the selection is real and we name it). The verdict does not
> hinge on the exact roster: it hinges on the fact that a 40-name survivor basket over 9 annual
> rebalances carries far too much sampling noise to certify a few-percent annual spread, and on
> the **sign** of what little signal there is.

## The signal — long-short by year (low issuance − high issuance)

1-year execution lag; equal-weight 30% tails. A positive L−S means the buyback (low-issuance)
names beat the diluting (high-issuance) names that year — the direction the factor predicts.

| formation year | long (low-issuance) | short (high-issuance) | L − S |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2016 | +37.1% | +30.8% | **+6.2%** |
| 2017 | +1.2% | +5.9% | −4.7% |
| 2018 | +36.2% | +39.2% | −3.0% |
| 2019 | +9.8% | +32.1% | **−22.2%** |
| 2020 | +41.2% | +29.6% | **+11.5%** |
| 2021 | −12.1% | −6.7% | −5.4% |
| 2022 | +20.1% | +44.8% | **−24.7%** |
| 2023 | +17.4% | +8.3% | +9.1% |
| 2024 | +26.2% | +25.7% | +0.5% |

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| n years | **9** |
| L−S mean | **−3.63% / yr** (median −2.97%) |
| win-rate | **44%** (4 of 9 years positive) |
| annual Sharpe | **−0.29** |
| one-sample *t* (vs 0) | **−0.86** |
| label-shuffle placebo *p* | **0.795** |

Read it carefully. The **sign is reversed** on this survivor tape: the low-issuance (buyback)
basket *underperformed* the high-issuance (diluting) basket by **−3.6%/yr** — the opposite of
the Pontiff-Woodgate prediction. The one-sample *t* is **−0.86** (nowhere near ∣t∣ ≥ 2), the
win-rate is a sub-coin-flip 44%, and the **label-shuffle placebo** says a random relabelling of
which name carries which issuance value beats the real sort **79%** of the time. There is no
edge here in either direction — only sampling noise around a slightly negative mean.

## Costs make a non-edge worse

| | L−S mean / yr | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| gross | −3.63% | −0.86 |
| net @ 10 bps × 2 legs + 50 bps borrow | **−4.33%** | −1.02 |

The annual two-sided rebalance plus a 50 bps short borrow shave another ~0.7pp off an already
negative spread. Costs are not the binding constraint — the binding constraint is that the gross
spread is **statistically indistinguishable from zero** (and slightly the wrong sign).

## Robustness — the sign and the noise are stable across cuts

**Quantile width sweep** (does the sort hold at other tail widths?):

| frac (tail) | n | L−S mean | *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.2 | 9 | −6.50% | −0.97 | −0.32 |
| 0.3 | 9 | −3.63% | −0.86 | −0.29 |
| 0.4 | 9 | −5.39% | −1.30 | −0.43 |

**Split-half by year:**

| sub-period | L−S mean | *t* | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| first half (2016–2020) | −2.44% | −0.42 | 5 |
| second half (2021–2024) | −5.12% | −0.71 | 4 |

Every cut is **negative and insignificant** — the spread is consistently the wrong sign for the
published factor and never within reach of *t* = 2. This is the texture of a *factor that does
not survive an honest small-survivor-basket replication*, not a sign-flipped real edge (a real
sign-flip would itself need ∣t∣ ≥ 2 to claim, and it has ∣t∣ ≤ 1.3 everywhere).

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and ~40 names / 9 years is the limit

Averaged over **25** deterministic synthetic worlds (seeds 519…543), with a **known planted
issuance edge** (low-issuance names earn ``edge`` more per year):

| planted edge | mean *t* (25 seeds) | L−S mean |
|---|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | **−0.11** | −0.6% |
| **+0.10** (large edge) | **+4.55** | +17.6% |

With **no** planted edge the averaged *t* sits at **−0.11** (no false positive — the sort cannot
manufacture significance from ~40 names over 9 years). Only a **large** planted edge (+10%/yr to
the buyback leg) drives the averaged *t* to **+4.55**. The control proves the measurement engine
is unbiased and correctly signed (a *real* low-issuance edge would print a clearly **positive**
*t*) — which makes the real-tape *t* of **−0.86** all the more telling: it is what *no edge* (or
a faint wrong-signed wobble) looks like through a 40-name / 9-year keyhole.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The long-short spread is **−3.6%/yr at *t* = −0.86** — the *wrong sign* for
  the Pontiff-Woodgate factor and far inside its own standard error. The label-shuffle placebo
  beats the real sort 79% of the time; the win-rate is 44%. The faithful synthetic control shows
  a *real* low-issuance edge would print a clearly positive *t*, so this is not a hidden
  sign-flipped edge — it is **noise**. Literature support cannot lift a wrong-signed,
  insignificant estimate to REAL. **Survivorship** in the 40-name basket is named on this axis.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A spread you cannot distinguish from zero (and that points the wrong
  way) is not a deployable book at any size; costs + borrow only make a non-edge worse
  (net −4.3%/yr). There is nothing to size.
- **"Does the published factor replicate here?" — BUSTED.** A canonical, pointed academic factor
  replicated honestly on a small survivor basket with real costs lands exactly where the desk
  expects the *most* of them to: the sign reverses, the *t* never clears 2, and a label-shuffle
  cannot be beaten. The effect that survives in CRSP's full point-in-time cross-section (with
  thousands of names, the small diluters included, and a proper factor model) **does not survive**
  a 40-name survivor replication — a textbook small-sample / survivorship illustration, not a
  free lunch.
